submitter: bugs_open/386 session — Phase 2 migration (arm fact-value history on five fundamentallyai counting facts)
rationale:
bugs_open/386 Phase 2. The CLM-028 reader/writer shipped and is LIVE at chassis v1.0.1339 (capability-probed at BOTH agent-chassis replicas' /proc/1/exe for `retain_history`, with a present-control `context_terms` FOUND and an absent-control found on neither). It was armed on nothing: zero facts fleet-wide carried the key. This migration arms the first five — fundamentallyai.com's F9-F13, the bug's own motivating case.

WHY THESE AND NOT THE OWNER'S 'at least N' RULING. §4b of the bug file rules that a counting fact is expressed as a floor or the claim cancelled, and explicitly preserves this mechanism for what the ruling cannot reach. F9-F13 have NO writer_line, so they contribute nothing to composeWriterBlock: their numbers reach the page through an evidence-chart component rendering the register into content_data, not through prose. There is no sentence to rephrase, only a chart — and the chart stamps its own 'verified 2026-08-23', so the rendered figure is a true statement for ever. The register simply could not agree with it.

THE HISTORY IS DERIVED IN SQL, NOT TYPED. Every value is computed in the file from this site's own superseded site_specs rows, applying exactly the rules recordFactHistory applies at runtime (consecutive duplicates collapsed, current value excluded, oldest first, capped at 90). The migration therefore CANNOT seed a value the register never held, which is the honesty property the whole mechanism rests on. A hardcoded array would have made that a promise; this makes it structural.

CONTROLS RUN BEFORE WRITING THE FILE, and one of them is what makes the rest mean anything. Baseline over 91 live components (export asserted 91 vs count(*), stderr empty): 5 findings, all capabilities/evidence-chart. Armed offline: 0. Disappeared: exactly those five, EVERY ONE on the register-rendering component, ZERO in free-text prose — the sharper acceptance test the `compliance` seat asked for on corr 18dba069, and the result that would have stopped this file. Appeared: none. NEGATIVE CONTROL: zero findings makes 'nothing else disappeared' trivially true, so a value the register has never held was injected into the same component (11513 -> 11514; the archive runs 11373, 11513, 11646, 11828) and rescanned against the armed register — STILL FLAGGED. One away from a genuinely-held value, identical context window, caught.

POST-APPLY, verified at the artefact rather than the status: the live register carries 16 facts (unchanged), exactly 5 armed, histories 30/30/31/30/12 entries each ending at that fact's last pre-current reading; claimscan against the LIVE register over the real pages returns 0 findings, down from 5; and the negative control against that same live register still flags 11514.

plan.summary: Supersede-then-insert fundamentallyai's current evidence_base, adding retain_history:true and a SQL-derived history array to five named facts. Every other fact and every unknown key carried verbatim; fact order preserved. Guards refuse a re-apply, a moved register, or an empty/over-cap derivation; the verify block runs inside the transaction as a DO that can abort.

edits.rationale: Supersede-then-insert rather than UPDATE, following 585/270 and writeRefreshedEvidenceBase, because idx_site_specs_current is UNIQUE on (site_id, aspect) WHERE is_current — two statements, one transaction, that order. History derived from superseded rows so no value can be invented. THE ARMED-ID FILTER IS LOAD-BEARING and was added after the runner's doomed-transaction probe caught its absence: without it the derivation produces history for every fact whose value has ever moved (F1-live-sites, F2-council-seats), and the file would have armed SEVEN facts while claiming five — the bulk-toggle the `guardian` seat's advisory on corr 18dba069 warns against. Caught by this file's own VERIFY block before any write, which is the argument for putting the assertions in the migration rather than in a runbook.
edits.sketch:
WITH armed(fid) AS (VALUES ('F9-…'),('F10-…'),('F11-…'),('F12-…'),('F13-…')),
     base AS (SELECT … ORDER BY superseded_at DESC LIMIT 1),
     raw  AS (… WHERE NOT is_current AND ss.id <> b.id AND f->>'id' IN (SELECT fid FROM armed)
              , lag(value) OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY created_at) AS prev),
     kept AS (… WHERE (prev IS NULL OR v <> prev) AND v <> curval),
     hist AS (SELECT fid, jsonb_agg(… ORDER BY created_at) WHERE rn_desc <= 90 GROUP BY fid)
INSERT … jsonb_set(jsonb_set(f,'{retain_history}','true'),'{history}',h.entries) … ORDER BY ord

edits.rationale: Strips both keys from every fact by the same supersede-then-insert route, with its own guard and verify. States the consequence plainly rather than implying the rollback is free: rolling back returns the five stale-render findings at error severity and makes that page refusable again.

grounded_in: Owner authorisation 2026-08-25, in session: 'go ahead and arm it'. Scope as ruled by the `guardian` seat on corr 18dba069 — arming is a one-fact-at-a-time reviewed operator act, never a bulk toggle. This file arms FIVE named facts on ONE site.

bug file §4b (owner ruling 2026-08-25, commit 2a9091c7d): counting facts are expressed as 'at least N' or cancelled — and candidate 1 'remains the durable fix and is not superseded by this ruling'. F9-F13 are the case the ruling cannot reach: no writer_line, so no prose to rephrase.
MEASURED 2026-08-25 post-apply: live register 16 facts, exactly 5 armed, history lengths 30/30/31/30/12, each ending at that fact's last pre-current value (11646, 10416, 437, 503, 23).
MEASURED 2026-08-25 at the artefact: claimscan over 91 live components against the LIVE armed register returns 0 findings (was 5, all capabilities/evidence-chart).

MEASURED 2026-08-25, the negative control against the LIVE armed register: a never-held 11514 injected one away from a genuinely-held 11513, same context window, is STILL FLAGGED. Arming spares the values the register held and nothing adjacent.

Chassis v1.0.1339 carries the reader: capability probe of `retain_history` at /proc/1/exe on both replicas, present-control `context_terms` FOUND, absent-control `zzz_not_a_real_symbol_386` absent on both. NOT dated from service_binary_capabilities, which the bugs_open/364 lane measured STALE for this very roll.
plan.risks:
1. FALSE-NEGATIVE SURFACE, bounded and measured rather than argued. Five facts now accept up to 30/30/31/30/12 additional exact values each, only inside their existing context_terms. The negative control shows an adjacent invented number (11514) is still caught, and the disappearing-findings diff shows nothing outside the five stale renders was spared. The residual risk is an invented figure that EXACTLY equals one of those historic readings in a matching window — for 5-digit counters negligible; for F13 (values 9-23) it is the real one, and F13 is the fact I would drop first if a reviewer objects.

2. THE WRITER HALF IS STILL UNEXERCISED. This file SEEDS history; it does not prove recordFactHistory writes it. The demand control is the next evidence-freshness tick that MOVES one of these five values: it should append the outgoing reading itself and report FactsHistoryRecorded > 0. Until then the writer is inferred from unit tests, not observed in production, and that is stated rather than glossed.

3. CHURN. Unchanged — this register already gains a superseded row per day from its sql-sourced facts. The history arrays add ~30 small objects to a 15KB document.

4. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. The bug class stays open for every unarmed counting fact. The only other genuinely exposed fact fleet-wide is leopardess C1-records-enriched (moves AND reaps, current value 937 is its own historic low), and it is a PROSE fact, so whether it takes a floor or history is a live question rather than a copy of this decision. bugs_open/386 stays OPEN and says so.
